This is a training question, not a pain one, so I'll answer in words. Let me check what you're doing now so I don't guess. Nothing is logged for deadlifts yet and you have no active program, so I'm going on general coaching here.

For a stronger lower back, the best additions are usually the ones that train the same hinge pattern with a bit more volume. Romanian deadlifts are the first one I'd add, since they build the hamstrings and spinal erectors under load. Next would be back extensions, done controlled, or good mornings if you're comfortable with them. A heavy row variation helps too, because upper back strength keeps you tight off the floor. Finish with some hard core bracing work, like planks or suitcase carries.

Most people do fine adding one or two of these after their deadlift day, around 3 sets of 8 to 12 with a weight that leaves a couple of reps in the tank.

If you'd like, I can build a program around the deadlift with these built in. Tell me how many days a week you can train and for how long.
